 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the injured petitioner is seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in M.V.C.No.18/2015 dated 06.02.2016 by the learned Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and Addl.M.A.C.T.-13 (Itinerary Court) at Shikaripura ('the Tribunal' in short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts as pleaded by the petitioner are, on 16.08.2014 at about 9.15 a.m., the petitioner while riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA-15/U-2967 on S.S road near Ambedkar circle, a MMS bus bearing No.KA- 14/A-1313 hit against the motor cycle causing him the injuries.
After taking treatment at Government Hospital, NC: 2023:KHC:34723 Shikaripura, seeking compensation, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal by impugned judgment, awarded Rs.1,09,240/- with 6% interest per annum.
Seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. I have heard the arguments of Sri.K.V.Sateeshchandra, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri.M.U.Poonacha, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurer.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that, as evident from Ex.P10/case sheet, the petitioner was hospitalized at McGann Hospital, Shivamogga from 16.08.2014 to 19.08.2014.
Though he has produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.9,390/-, the Tribunal has not considered and awarded meager amount.
The Tribunal has further committed an error in taking the income at Rs.4,000/- per month.
The compensation NC: 2023:KHC:34723 awarded towards loss of future income is also on the lower, which requires to be re-assessed.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the wound certificate speaks that the injuries are simple.
Though the petitioner has claimed Rs.9,390/- towards medical expenses, there are no prescriptions produced, hence, the Tribunal is correct in discarding it.

Tribunal has awarded fair compensation and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of both parties and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner and his entitlement to claim the compensation.
The compensation shall neither be inadequate nor a bonanza.
As the accident was of the year 2014, the notional income at Rs.8,500/- per month has to be assessed for a person with no proof of income.
The nature of injury will certainly impact the petitioner and he has to laid up for about five months.
The loss of income during laid-up period will come to Rs.42,500/-.
Only on the guise of absence of prescriptions, the Tribunal discounting the medical bills is not proper as the petitioner was inpatient.

When he was admitted as inpatient,
prescriptions cannot be expected for each and every bill.
Hence, discounted bills has to be paid to the petitioners.

The claim is based on a social legislation, the evidence on record speaks of nature of injury,
which requires hospitalization and the pain and agony underwent by the petitioner.
Full medical bills of Rs.10,000/- is accepted.
A sum of Rs.30,000/- is assessed towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

The treated doctor has opined that the petitioner has suffered 27% disability to left shoulder and 9% to whole body, it is appropriate to assess 10% disability for assessing the compensation towards loss of future income, which comes to Rs.71,400/- (Rs.8,500/-x12x7x10%).

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under following heads:
 As awarded As awarded  by the by this Court  Compensation under Tribunal  different Heads (Rs.)
 (Rs.)
Pain and sufferings 30,000/- 30,000/-
Medical expenses 5,000/- 10,000/-
Food and nourishment 6,000/- 6,000/-
Attendant charges 6,000/- 6,000/-
Elumalai vs Bangarappa on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191064030/
3  NC: 2023:KHC:34723 Travelling expenses 5,000/- 5,000/-
Loss of income during laid- 12,000/- 42,500/-
up period Loss of amenities 15,000/- 30,000/-
Loss of future income 30,240/- 71,400/-

Total 1,09,240/- 2,00,900/-
In all, the petitioner is entitled to Rs.2,00,900/- as against Rs.1,09,240/- assessed by the Tribunal,
thereby enhancement of Rs.91,660/- to which the petitioner is entitled.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment is modified.

iii) The petitioner would be entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.91,660/-
with interest of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation excluding interest for the delayed period of 97 days in filing the appeal.
NC: 2023:KHC:34723 iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records.
